notes.title: Labyrinthatory is now Steam Deck Verified!
notes.notes: [p]Steam just gave us the news: Labyrinthatory is now Steam Deck verified! Have fun puzzling on the go to your heart's content.[/p][p]As always, let us know what feedback you have. We're happy to make changes and improvements. In the meantime, we hope you enjoy update v1.1![/p]

notes.title: Labyrinthatory 1.1 Update Now Out!
notes.notes:
Thanks so much for supporting our weird little game! 
We're happy to release this patch with some quality-of-life tweaks, fun extras, and groundwork for future improvements. We’ll continue listening to your feedback!

[b]New Content[/b]
- Added a hidden extra room on the main floor to help track achievements.

[b]Options Menu[/b]
- Added an option to disable screen shake.
- Added an option to swap dialogue voices for text box SFX sounds.

[b]Gameplay Tweaks[/b]
- Base Roxanne’s movement speed increased by ~15% for smoother pacing.
- Color Sudoku now starts you out with more tiles.
- Sprinkled in some more “Fun Facts of the Day” to make the achievement easier.

[b]Technical Updates[/b]
- Engine changes for better Steam Deck compatibility.
- Updated gamepad logic for improved analog stick mouse control.
- Touchscreen support added on Steam Deck.

[b]Fixes[/b]
- Numerous bug fixes and stability improvements.
- Numerous typo fixes across the game.

notes.title: Nominate Labyrinthatory for "Best Game You Suck At"
notes.notes: We invite you to nominate Labyrinthatory for this year's "Best Game You Suck At" award as part of the 2023 Steam Awards. The game has 60 puzzles featuring a Stupid Hard mode, so you can crank up the difficulty for a fun challenge across a variety of knowledge and skill domains. Granted, it's no Souls-like game, but everyone has at least one puzzle they suck at, making Labyrinthatory a solid contender as a game everyone sucks at...at least a little.

notes.title: Livestream of Labyrinthatory with Development Team
notes.notes: We'll be playing Labyrinthatory as a development team live on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/broadcast/watch/76561199379179045]Steam[/url] at 8:30pm MDT on Saturday, October 14th as part of Steam Next Fest. We'll try playing through large parts of the game without showing off anything too spoiler-y. Our technical director (Jacob), assistant technical director (Erika), and art director (Brooke) will provide commentary as our CEO (Tom) plays through the game. (He might cheat to show more cool stuff off.) Come see many of our 80+ puzzles and other game features and let us know what you think!
